messages:
incidents-bot: [alert] gpu.xid.surge detected on gpu-node-57 (10.0.57.12) — Xid 31 repeat errors, pod restarts observed. Paging on-call :rotating_light:

sasha: paging @mike-oncall — grafana shows a spike starting 08:12 UTC, ~120 Xid 31s in 3m, k8s shows multiple inference pods OOMKilled. Can you pick this up?

mike-oncall: taking it. oncall->incident. I'm attaching recent dmesg snippets and driver log.

priya: seeing client error surge 502s on /v1/generate for hosted API routes to model-xlarge in us-west-2. Router latency jumped to 600ms then timeouts. Customers: small subset of PLG apps.

mike-oncall: quick triage — ssh to gpu-node-57. dmesg shows repeated: 
```
NVRM: Xid (31): PID 21234: Xid 31, GPU has fallen off the bus.
NVRM: Xid (31): GPU appears to have stopped responding, resetting the driver!
```
Also kernel log: `nvhost: GPU reset called due to HANG` and ECC corrected errors increasing.

devon: hopping in. Any recent maintenance or firmware push?

calvin: no recent driver rolls in us-west-2. Last infra agent update 3 days ago. Telemetry shows corrected ECC count rising on gpu2 of that node.

mike-oncall: mitigation plan proposal: 1) cordon + drain node, 2) migrate critical inference pods to standby capacity (prefer dedicated fallback pool), 3) if drain pods keep restarting due to driver resets, evict using --force; 4) repro & collect nv-host logs, enable verbose driver logging, 5) open customer comms if impact persists >30m. Thoughts?

priya: prioritize moving traffic away from that node / model variant. Can we flip routing to model-xlarge-quantized fallback for affected routes to keep latency low?

sasha: yes — switching routing at the gateway to fallback variant now for affected customer tag `org:plg-beta`. Rolling update should finish in ~45s.

incidents-bot: Action logged: routing override applied for model-xlarge -> model-xlarge-quantized for org:plg-beta by sasha.

mike-oncall: starting cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-57` -> Cordon succeeded. Beginning drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-57 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

devon: observing pods evicted but some come back with CrashLoopBackOff with reasons: `OOMKilled` followed by immediate Xid reset during init. Suggest we set `spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` lower and force delete remaining pods after snapshotting logs.

mike-oncall: doing log grab: `journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200 > /tmp/gpu-node-57-driver.log` and `kubectl logs -n inference --tail=200 pod/infer-xyz > /tmp/pod-infer-xyz.log`

dena: I can spawn warm standby capacity (dedicated-gpu-warmpool) and pre-pull models to absorb new load. Warming now.

mike-oncall: drain progress: 6 of 8 pods evicted, 2 stuck (kubelet keeps restarting container due to driver reset at start). Will force delete and let scheduler reschedule to warmpool.

sasha: noted customer impact: ~120 requests/min failing for org:plg-beta, default retry gives some success. Opening internal customer-impact doc and pinging SEs.

priya: telemetry note: KV-cache hit ratio dropping during restarts, causing more cold-start tokens which increase mem pressure. Consider lowering per-pod concurrency to reduce memory pressure on target nodes.

mike-oncall: executed `kubectl delete pod infer-stuck-1 --force --grace-period=0` -> pod gone. New pod scheduled on dedicated-gpu-warmpool-03, started successfully.

incidents-bot: oncall handoff scheduled in 25m to @devops-team. Add follow-up to run extended stress tests on spare node.

calvin: can we repro in lab? I'll reserve a node and run `stress-ng --matrix` + model load to try to trigger ECC increments. If we can repro, we can validate whether it's ECC-correctable accumulation leading to resets.

devon: good call. Meanwhile, operational steering: increase eviction threshold for `driver-reset` alerts to avoid noisy paging, but keep hard paging path for sustained >200 Xid/min.

mike-oncall: customer comms draft: "We observed GPU driver resets causing transient errors for inference endpoints in us-west-2. Traffic for affected customers has been routed to fallback model variants and we are draining the impacted host. We will follow up once the node is fully evacuated and telemetry stabilizes." Sending to growth/SEs for review.

priya: update: latency for fallback routes ~200-250ms — acceptable. Errors for org:plg-beta down to ~5/min. Nice work.

mike-oncall: node evacuated. Running `nvidia-smi -q` shows GPU memory returns normal but corrected ECC count high: `Volatile: 1345` corrected errors. I'm leaning toward hardware-level ECC saturation. Plan: quarantine node (mark as cordoned, add label `quarantine=ecc-suspect`) and schedule replacement/maintenance window.

sasha: label applied. Also adding host to quarantine pool: `kubectl label node gpu-node-57 quarantine=ecc-suspect maint-ticket=INC-2026`

devon: filing hardware ticket with rack ops — include NVML logs, corrected ECC counts, and dmesg. Recommend immediate replacement of GPU or board after confirmation.

mike-oncall: handoff notes for next oncall: node evacuated, traffic routed to fallback model variants for affected orgs, customer-impact doc shared (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-comm), logs collected at /var/lib/incident/gpu-node-57/*. Please monitor Xid alert state; if Xid spikes resume escalate to SRE lead.

calvin: repro job queued in lab. I'll post results in this thread. If we can replicate via ECC stress test, open bug against nv-driver with collected repro.

dena: warmpool absorbed additional load fine. Scaling down warmpool after 30m stable.

mike-oncall: closing incident paging for now. Leaving node quarantined. Will follow up with postmortem after hardware ticket completes. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident resolved for alert gpu.xid.surge on gpu-node-57 — automated route overrides removed after 30m stability.

calvin: lab repro failure: couldn't trigger Xid 31 with stress test; suggests corrupted memory on that host only. Raised with HW ops.

devon: follow-up action items: ["replace GPU on gpu-node-57", "add preemptive ECC threshold alerts per zone", "run kvcache memory tuning for high-cold-start workloads"].

mike-oncall: ack. Handoff complete.
